newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Chronology of N.Korean ideologue's defection drama.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of N.Korean ideologue's defection drama.

text.p: Hwang Jang-yop, the highest-ranking North Korean to flee the Stalinist state, arrived in South Korea on Sunday, more than two months after he sought political asylum.
The following is a chronology of the main developments in the saga:
Jan 30 - Hwang visits Japan on lecture tour to promote North Korea's ideology of "juche", or self-reliance, which he helped author.
Feb 11 - Hwang arrives in Beijing on his way home.
Feb 12 - Hwang and his aide Kim Duk-hong walk into Seoul consulate seeking political asylum. North Korean cars park outside the diplomatic compound.

Feb 13 - South Korea sends envoy to Beijing to negotiate Hwang's release, but he is rebuffed. North Korea accuses Seoul of kidnapping Hwang. Seoul releases memo it says Hwang wrote expressing his wish to go to Seoul and discuss national reunification.
Feb 14 - South Korean foreign minister Yoo Chong-ha meets his Chinese counterpart Qian Qichen in Singapore. Qian says Beijing needs time to investigate Hwang's case.
Feb 15 - Prominent North Korean defector fatally shot outside Seoul, and South Korean authorities say they are seeking two suspected Pyongyang hitmen.
Feb 17 - North Korea says if Hwang genuine defector, he is a renegade and will be dismissed.
Feb 19 - Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping dies. Mourning delays talks on Hwang's fate.
March 14 - Chinese Premier Li Peng says conditions "nearly ripe" for solving Hwang problem.
March 18 - Hwang leaves Beijing for the Philippines. China demands that Hwang must stay in the Philippines for about a month before going to Seoul.
March 26 - The Philippines has told China and South Korea it will provide sanctuary to Hwang for as short a time as possible.
April 2 - President Fidel Ramos said he had agreed to a joint request by South Korea and China to extend North Korean defector's stay in the Philippines for a month.
April 17 - Security officials in Seoul say Hwang will arrive in Seoul by April 22.
April 19 - Seoul government officials confirm Hwang will arrive in South Korea on April 20 on a special plane.
April 20 - Hwang and his aide Kim arrive in South Korea.
